newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SingTel cuts handphone rates as competition grows.
newsitem.headline: SingTel cuts handphone rates as competition grows.

text.p: Singapore Telecommunications Ltd (SingTel) said on Thursday it would cut charges for mobile telephone calls and provide improved service features starting May 1.
In a statement, SingTel Mobile unveiled price reductions for new and existing customers.
The new pricing would enable customers to save up to seven percent in monthly subscriptions, 20 percent in call charges and get more than 40 percent free talk time, it said.
It would also lower charges for incoming calls, making it more affordable for customers to be contacted on mobile phones.
Customers would also obtain free value-added services such as call forward, call barring, call waiting and conference calls for up to six parties, it said.
The statement quoted the chief executive officer of SingTel Mobile, Lung Chien Ping, as saying the strategy was "not to compete based on price alone but to provide value to customers."
Singapore's handphone market was deregulated on April 1, allowing one new competitor, MobileOne (M1), to compete for the first time against the 82 percent government-owned former monopoly, SingTel.
M1 told Reuters in an interview earlier on Thursday it had already grabbed almost 10 percent of the local handphone market in only three weeks of operations.
M1 is a joint venture of Singapore Press Holdings, Keppel Telecom, Britain's Cable & Wireless and Hong Kong Telecommunications.

SingTel shares on Thursday plunged to a record low of Singapore $2.50 before recovering to $2.54 by the close, down eight cents on the day. Analysts and brokerage dealers said the falls were spurred by the success of its rival.
